docs.text:
1. Go to GitHub Releases and download the latest Windows package (e.g., MusicScoreManager-Windows-vX.Y.Z.zip or the installer).
  2. Extract the ZIP archive to your preferred directory (e.g., C:\Program Files\MusicScoreManager or your user folder).
  3. Double-click MusicScoreManager.exe to launch the application. (Optional: right-click the executable to create a Desktop shortcut or pin it to your Taskbar).

docs.title: 🛠️ For Developers: Building from Source (.NET MAUI)
docs.text:
For developers who want to compile and customize the application for Android or Windows:

  1. Install the .NET 10 SDK and .NET MAUI workloads: 
    dotnet workload install maui
dotnet workload install maui-android
dotnet workload install maui-windows
  2. Clone the official Git repository: 
    git clone https://github.com/Audiothor/MusicScoreManager.git
cd MusicScoreManager
  3. Build according to the desired target:

dotnet build -t:Run -f net10.0-android

# For Android: generate signed Release APK package
dotnet publish -f net10.0-android -c Release

# For Windows: compile Windows executable
dotnet build -f net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0 -c Release

dotnet publish -f net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0 -c Release

docs.title: Quick Start Guide (Get Started in 5 Minutes)
docs.text: Welcome to Music Score Manager! This guide walks you step-by-step through setting up, importing your first scores, and being ready to play on stage or in rehearsal in just a few minutes.

docs.title: At a Glance: The 5 Essential Steps
docs.text:
1. Import scores
  2. Organize tags
  3. View the score
  4. Add annotations
  5. Create a Live Setlist and run it

docs.title: Step 1: Import Your First Scores
docs.text:
As soon as the app opens, go to the Scores menu (in the navigation bar).

  1. Tap the + button located at the top right.
  2. The file picker opens: select one or more sheet music PDF or Image files (JPEG, PNG).
  3. You have 2 ways to import scores:
  4. Copy into the application (i.e. local mode) your selected score(s). This is the recommended solution!
  5. Base yourself on your source file without copying it into the app. This solution is NOT recommended because if files are moved, you will always need external access to your scores. Music Score Manager can easily manage several hundred scores locally.
  6. In the case of a PDF file:
  7. The file is immediately integrated into your library.
  8. A modern window appears with the 🎵 Open score button to play it right away!
  9. In the case of photos or images:
  10. The application offers to automatically convert them to PDF format.
  11. If you select multiple photos (e.g. photos of individual pages of a piece), the application offers to merge them into 1 single multi-page PDF score.
  12. Your score(s) are listed and accessible in the Scores menu: simply click on one to open it.

[!TIP] Storage Advice: By default, the application copies files into its secure local storage. Your scores remain 100% accessible offline, without ever depending on the Internet or a Cloud network.

docs.title: Step 2: Organize Your Library with Folders and Tags
docs.text:
To find your pieces instantly among hundreds of scores:

  1. Folders & Categories (Thematic Organization):
  2. Toggle seamlessly between Classic List View and Folders View at any time using the 📁 button at the top of the screen.
  3. Assign each score to a folder (e.g. Classical, Jazz, Choir, Studies...) from its edit screen or via the 3-dots context menu 📁 Change folder. Create new folders on the fly with the ➕ button.
  4. Color-Coded Tags (Cross-Category Labels):
  5. Create your own tags with custom colors via Tools > Tag Management (or Settings > Score Settings > Manage Tag List).
  6. A score can have multiple tags simultaneously (e.g. Vocals, Piano, Christmas).
  7. Edit Musical Metadata:
  8. In Scores, tap the three little dots ⋮ on a score, then choose Edit score.
  9. Set the title, composer, folder category, tags, key signature, starting tempo, and star rating.
  10. Don't forget to tap Save!
  11. Use the search bar at the top to filter instantly by Title, Composer, or filter by Folder and Tags.

docs.title: Step 3: Use the Score Viewer
docs.text:
Simply tap a score in the list to launch the Full-Screen Viewer.

  • Turning Pages:
  • Swipe / Tap: Swipe or tap the right third of the screen to go forward (next page), the left third to go backward (previous page).
  • Wireless Foot Pedal:
  • Pair your Bluetooth pedal (AirTurn, PageFlip, Donner, etc.). Page turns work immediately out of the box. You can also customize each pedal switch in Settings!
  • Show / Hide Controls:
  • Double-tap the center of the screen to show the quick actions menu (rotations, 100% zoom reset, jump to page...).
  • Tap the bottom of the screen to show the annotation toolbar (featuring a dedicated vertical pan handle ⠿).
  • Tap the top-right corner of the screen (or the [ 🛠️ ] icon) to open the Quick Tools Drawer: toggle the metronome, audio backing track player, annotations, top title bar, page numbers, and the floating High-Precision Multi-Instrument Tuner in one tap!
  • Exit the current score:
  • Open the central menu (double-tap) and choose « Return to Home ».

docs.title: Step 4: Annotate the Score (Pencil, Highlighter, Text & Stickers)
docs.text:
In score reading mode, tap the bottom of the screen to deploy the toolbox:

  • 🖌️ Highlighter (Stabilo): Highlight measures with translucent colors (yellow, green, pink, blue, orange) in fine or wide strokes.
  • ✎ Pencil: Write freehand annotations, fingerings, drawings, or slurs (size and color of your choice).
  • T Text: Insert readable text notes directly onto the staff.
  • ❏ Musical Stickers: Access over 100 symbols classified by category (Dynamics p, f, crescendo, breaths, fingerings, repeats D.C., Coda...). Drag them where you want on the score or double-click for them to position above the staff. By going to the Settings > Annotation Settings menu, you can create your Favorite Stickers which you will find in the stickers/Favorites annotations.
  • ↩ Undo / ↪ Redo: Undo or redo your changes at any time.
  • Any annotation can be deleted or moved.

[!TIP] Locking: For safety, a small padlock prevents accidental manipulation errors with annotations. In green, modifications are allowed. A closed bar or a padlock in red prevents any modification.

docs.title: Step 5: Create a Setlist for a Rehearsal or Concert
docs.text:
Stop searching for your sheets one by one between pieces on stage: prepare your program!

  1. Go to the Setlists tab.
  2. Tap + at the top right, give it a name (e.g. Electro Concert at the Castle) and confirm.
  3. Tap + Add to pick your pieces from your library.
  4. Reorganize the order of songs simply by drag and drop.
  5. For any modifications, don't forget to save!
  6. Tap one of your scores in this list to start your concert at that spot, or go to the Setlists tab and click on the concert you want: the viewer opens on the first piece. At the end of the last page of the score, it automatically moves to the next piece according to the Setlist settings you selected!
  7. The setlist drawer lets you view upcoming pieces at any time (top center).

docs.title: Step 6: Practical Built-in Tools (Metronome & Audio Player)
docs.text:
Directly from the score viewer (or in score editing):

  • Built-in Metronome:
  • Adjust tempo (BPM).
  • Choose between a discrete sound or a flashing visual signal without sound (ideal in concert).
  • Accompanying Audio Player:
  • Link an audio file (MP3, WAV, AAC, FLAC) to a score to rehearse with the backing track or demo.
  • Control playback (Play / Pause, return to beginning) directly from the score viewer.

and many others...

In the Tools tab you will find numerous utilities to help you:

  • Sharing between musicians: Use the Wi-Fi Direct P2P menu to transmit a complete setlist with annotations to a person or even to your fellow musicians backstage, very quickly, even without an Internet connection!
  • Import files (which already include annotations that you or someone else exported to you).
  • Duplicate management, practical when you have several hundred scores.
  • Backups.
  • Assembly and internal organization of your scores (you can redefine the orientation and order of your PDF pages!).

In the Settings tab you will find plenty of customization options for the application across all menus.

docs.title: 🚪 Quit Menu
docs.text: The Quit menu provides a clean and safe exit from the application.

docs.title: 🔒 Safe Exit Workflow
docs.text:
When you tap the Quit (🚪) tab in the bottom navigation bar:

  1. Confirmation Prompt (Optional):
  2. If enabled in settings, a confirmation prompt asks you to verify before exiting the application.
  3. Session State Persistence:
  4. The application automatically commits any pending changes, active filters, last viewed scores, and SQLite database transactions to disk.
  5. Resource & Memory Cleanup:
  6. PDF rendering buffers, background audio threads, and hardware resources are gracefully freed to optimize device battery life.
  7. Graceful App Termination:
  8. A brief status animation confirms disk writes are complete before closing the application cleanly with zero risk of database corruption.

docs.title: ⚙️ Settings Customization
docs.text: Under Settings > App Settings (General), the Application Behavior section includes two customization switches: - Show « Quit » tab in bottom navigation: Toggle to hide this tab if you navigate via Android system gestures or your device's physical back button. - Confirm Before Quitting: Protects against accidental exits with a confirmation alert.

docs.title: 🎵 Scores Menu
docs.text: The Scores menu is the primary gateway to your digital sheet music library. It displays all your scores in a responsive, modern card grid optimized for large tablets and phones alike.

docs.title: 🖥️ Top Header Elements & Controls
docs.text:
At the top of the scores view, you have immediate access to several critical tools:

  1. Real-time Search Bar:
  2. Type a few letters to instantly filter your library by piece title, composer name, or file name.

  3. Fast one-tap clear button to quickly return to your full catalog.

  4. View Mode Toggle Button (📁 Folders ⇄ List):

  5. Seamlessly switches between Classic List View and Folders / Categories View:

    • Folders Overview View: Displays category directories as lightweight preview cards with live score count badges. Tapping any folder opens its songs in an instantaneous drill-down view with breadcrumb navigation [ ⬅ All Folders ].
    • Folder Context Menu: Easily rename, empty, or delete any category (scores are safely moved to the default "Général" category).
    • Instant Creation: Tap [ ➕ New folder ] to create a new category immediately.
    • Scores are physically organized in dedicated sub-directories on storage under each folder name.

  6. Tag Filter Button (🏷️):

  7. Opens the tag selection modal with internal tag search and tag sort (A-Z, Z-A, most/least used).
  8. Displays active filters in a horizontal carousel with color pills and quick-remove buttons.

  9. « Clear all » and « Apply » buttons.

  10. Sort Order Selector (⇅):

  11. Instantly reorders your library by:

    • Date added (Newest first): Default sorting to easily find your latest imports.
    • Date added (Oldest first).
    • Title (A-Z) / Title (Z-A).
    • Modification date (Recently edited).
    • Rating (Highest rated): Pieces with 1 to 5 stars listed in descending order.
    • Composer (A-Z): Alphabetical composer order. A dedicated toggle in Settings > Scores controls whether pieces without a composer appear at the very top or at the end.
    • Untagged pieces first: Prioritizes scores with no assigned tags so you can quickly organize them.

  12. Batch Multi-selection Button (☑️):

  13. Activates bulk selection mode to perform operations across multiple scores simultaneously.

  14. Reveals an action bar at the bottom:

    • 🗑️ Batch Delete: Secure bulk deletion with confirmation prompt.
    • 📁 Folder Assignment: Modern modal to move or assign all checked scores to an existing or newly created folder at once.
    • 🏷️ Assign Tags: Modal overlay to add or replace tags across all selected scores at once.
    • 📦 Export Package (.msmscores): Generates a single compressed archive bundling all selected scores (with options to include annotations and audio backing tracks).
    • 📡 Share via Wi-Fi Direct: Send the entire batch over local peer-to-peer Wi-Fi without internet.

  15. Add Score Button (➕):

  16. Contextual Direct Import: When inside a specific folder, imported files are automatically saved directly into that category.
  17. PDF Import: Strict binary %PDF- verification prevents corrupt or misnamed files from crashing the viewer.
  18. Photos / Images Import & Conversion: Selecting one or more image files (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WEBP, BMP) informs the user that the selected image files will be converted into PDF format:
    • Cancel: Image files are ignored. Any accompanying PDF files in the same batch continue their normal import.
    • Continue: A loading overlay with progress status informs the user during high-definition PDF conversion. Images are merged into a single multi-page PDF score or created as individual PDF scores, and a completion alert is displayed once finished.

docs.title: 📥 Import Process & Storage Strategy
docs.text:
When importing scores, the app offers two flexible storage modes:

  • Copy to app library (Recommended): Copies the PDF into Music Score Manager's sandboxed storage directory. Scores stay accessible even if the original download folder is cleaned up or files are moved.
  • Link external original file (External): Retains the absolute path on storage without duplicating the file, marked by a blue 🔗 badge.

docs.title: 🗂️ Score Card Breakdown
docs.text: Every score is displayed as an informative card: - Piece Title. - Customizable Subtitle (configurable in Settings: composer name, date added, number of pages, or folder/category badge 📁 [FolderName]). - Color-coded Tag Badges for instant visual classification. - 🔗 External Linked File Badge when stored in custom external folders. - ⚠️ Missing File Warning Indicator (Red Exclamation Mark (!)): If a PDF file was moved or deleted from storage, a bright red warning badge appears to the left of the 3-dots ⋮ button, notifying you before a concert that the score cannot be opened. - Fast-Scroller Alphabetical Index (A-Z): A vertical alphabet bar on the right side of the list allows instant jumps to any letter with a single tap. - Floating Scroll-to-Top Button (▲): Returns instantly to the top of the library after long scrolling.

docs.title: ⋮ Context Menu (3 dots)
docs.text:
Tapping the ⋮ button on any score card opens the full context actions menu:

  1. 📖 Open score:

  2. Opens the score directly in the full-screen stage performance viewer.

  3. ✏️ Edit score:

  4. Opens the detailed metadata editor (ScoreEditPage):

    • Title & Composer / Arranger.
    • Folder / Category (with on-the-fly folder creation ➕).
    • Musical Key (both standard notation A, B, C... and classical solfège Do, Ré, Mi...).
    • Target Tempo (BPM): Automatically initializes the metronome when opening this score.
    • Star Rating (1 to 5 stars).
    • Dynamic Tag Selection.
    • Metronome Accordion: Time signature (2/4, 3/4, 4/4, 6/8...), subdivision, pre-count measures, and default mute/sound toggle.
    • Audio Tracks Accordion: Attach backing audio tracks (MP3, WAV, etc.), preview listening, and relative volume adjustment.
    • Technical File Details: Full path, file size, modification date, and button to re-link files if moved.

  5. 📋 Add to Setlist:

  6. Inserts the score immediately into the chosen setlist.
  7. High-priority 1st position placement (automatically shifts other songs down).

  8. Handles deduplication and confirmation if the setlist is locked.

  9. 📁 Change folder / category:

  10. Opens the modern category modal with glowing 📁 halo to move the score to another folder or create a new folder on the fly.

  11. 📑 Modify PDF assembly:

  12. Launches the piece directly inside the PDF Assembler Studio to rearrange pages, insert blank sheets, rotate pages, or remove unwanted sheets.

  13. 📡 Send via Wi-Fi Direct:

  14. Opens the sharing options modal asking you to choose:
    • ☑️ Include handwritten annotations & drawings.
    • ☑️ Include attached audio backing tracks (MP3/WAV).

  15. Starts high-speed P2P Wi-Fi Direct transfer to nearby devices.

  16. 📦 Export score (.msmscore):

  17. Produces a self-contained archive file containing the PDF, metadata, and optional annotations/audio.

  18. 🏷️ Rename score:

  19. Fast dialog shortcut to rename the piece without opening the full editor.

  20. 🗑️ Delete score:

  21. Removes the piece from your library with a safety confirmation prompt.

docs.title: 📋 Setlists Menu
docs.text: The Setlists menu is specially designed for planning, organizing, and executing your concert programs, auditions, church services, and rehearsals without downtime.

docs.title: 📋 Presentation & List Layout
docs.text: The Setlists tab displays all your created programs: - Top Toolbar: Real-time search, multi-criteria sort (Name A-Z/Z-A, Creation Date, Status), and fast creation button (➕). - Horizontal Status Filters: - All - Active (green badge): Programs currently being toured or practiced. - Upcoming (orange badge): Planned future concerts. - Completed (gray badge): Archived past performances. - Setlist Cards: - Program title, creation date, status pill, and lock padlock 🔒. - Swipe gestures for immediate access to Rename and Delete.

docs.title: ▶️ Instant Stage Start (One-Tap on Card)
docs.text: In Music Score Manager, going on stage is instantaneous: - A single tap on a setlist card launches the first score directly in the fullscreen stage viewer. - If the setlist is empty, a helpful message guides you to add scores to it. - During performance, the setlist activates continuous reading mode: when you turn the last page of a piece, the app automatically transitions to the first page of the next piece!

docs.title: 📋 Live Setlist Progress Drawer (v2.0.1.1)
docs.text: While playing scores from a setlist inside the viewer: - Discreet Top Edge Opening: A single tap at the top-center of the screen (invisible touch bar) smoothly slides down the progress drawer pinned to the top of the display. - Instant Automatic Centering: Upon opening, the drawer automatically scrolls to center the currently played song in the list. - Dedicated Visual Status Palette: - Currently playing score: High-contrast midnight blue background, cyan glowing outline, vibrant green ▶ badge, bright white title, and « Now Playing » cyan label. - Passed scores: Sage green checkmark ✓ (#52B788), muted bluish-gray text (#8A95A5), and « Passed » label. - Upcoming scores: Pastel blue number (#74C0FC), soft off-white text (#EAF2FF), composer in azure (#A5C8E4), and « Upcoming » label (#4DABF7). - Direct Navigation & Easy Dismissal: - Tap any piece in the drawer to jump directly and immediately to it. - Close the drawer via the ✕ cross button, by tapping the semi-transparent backdrop, or by clicking the current song.

docs.title: ⋮ Context Menu (3 dots)
docs.text:
Each setlist provides its own action menu via the ⋮ button:

  1. ▶️ Start setlist:

  2. Launches stage mode starting on the first song in full screen.

  3. ✏️ Edit setlist:

  4. Opens the editor (SetlistEditPage):

    • Title, Status & Concert Date: Set program title, status badge, and planned performance date.
    • Ultra-Fast Score Addition: Add songs with instant search, sorting, and folder/category filter button [📁] to quickly target a repertoire.
    • Reordering & Management: Reorder songs using ▲ / ▼ buttons (or drag-and-drop) and remove songs with the trash icon.
    • Collapsible « Advanced Options »: Toggle setlist-specific continuous mode, assign a dedicated Bluetooth pedal profile (takes priority during this concert and restores default on exit), or safely delete the setlist.

  5. 📡 Send via Wi-Fi Direct:

  6. Transmits the entire setlist and all its score files to other musicians' tablets via direct local streaming without internet.

  7. Options modal:

    • ☑️ Include handwritten annotations.
    • ☑️ Include attached audio backing tracks.

  8. 📦 Export (.msmsetlist):

  9. Generates a standalone .msmsetlist package containing the entire program, page order, PDFs, and optional annotations/audios.

  10. 📑 Duplicate setlist:

  11. Instantly clones the setlist with all pieces preserved in their exact order (ideal for variations of concert programs).

  12. 🏷️ Rename:

  13. Fast dialog to rename the setlist.

  14. 🔒 Lock / Unlock:

  15. Locks the setlist into Stage Mode to prevent accidental deletions or modifications during a concert.

  16. 🗑️ Delete:

  17. Deletes the setlist (your original scores remain completely safe in your library).

docs.title: ⚙️ Settings Menu
docs.text: The Settings menu (SettingsPage) allows you to precisely configure Music Score Manager for your instruments, stage performance habits, and display size.

docs.title: 🎵 1. Score Settings
docs.text:
The SettingsScoresPage page configures global sheet music library behaviors:

  • Default Sort on Launch:
  • Set which order applies automatically (Date added newest/oldest, Title A-Z/Z-A, Modification date, Star rating, Composer A-Z, or Untagged first).
  • Default View Mode (List vs Folders):
  • Choose whether the scores library opens by default in Classic List View or in Folders / Categories View.
  • Default Import Mode (Local Copy vs External Link):
  • Configure the default file handling when adding new scores: Copy to library (recommended) or Link original file (external).
  • Scores Without Composer First (Toggle On/Off):
  • When sorting by composer, choose whether pieces lacking a composer appear at the very top (On) or at the end of the alphabetical list (Off, default).
  • Score Subtitle Display:
  • Customize and reorder the information shown under each title in the library using interactive drag-and-drop or ▲ / ▼ buttons (Date added, Composer, Page count, Folder / Category 📁 [FolderName]), with individual checkboxes and real-time live preview.
  • Fast-Scroller Alphabetical Index (Toggle On/Off):
  • Displays or hides the vertical A-Z alphabet bar along the right edge of the score catalog.
  • Floating Scroll-to-Top Button (▲) (Toggle On/Off):
  • Displays or hides the circular floating button that scrolls back to the very top in one tap.
  • Current Page Number Display (Toggle On/Off):
  • Show or hide the bottom-right page index badge (e.g., Page 3 / 12).
  • Page Number Font Size:
  • Adjustable slider from 10 px to 40 px with live text size preview.
  • Show Toolbox Icon Top-Right (Toggle On/Off, default Off):
  • Displays or hides the visual [ 🛠️ ] button in the top-right corner. The secret touch hotspot opening the drawer remains active regardless of this setting.
  • Show Score Title at Top (Toggle On/Off):
  • Displays or hides the subtle top banner showing the current piece title in the viewer.
  • 2-Page Landscape Display (Toggle On/Off):
  • Enables side-by-side dual page reading on horizontal tablets with complete geometric annotation projection.
  • Keep Screen Awake While Reading (Toggle On/Off):
  • Prevents the device screen from dimming or falling asleep while viewing a score during rehearsal or live performance.
  • Ergonomic Page Turn Gestures:
  • Next page gesture: Swipe left, Tap right, or Swipe up.
  • Previous page gesture: Swipe right, Tap left, or Swipe down.
  • Organisation (Manage Tags):
  • Direct shortcut to the tag management console (TagsPage) to create, recolor, rename, or delete library tags.

docs.title: 📋 2. Setlist Settings
docs.text:
The SettingsSetlistsPage page governs live concert behaviors:

  • Continuous Reading by Default (Toggle On/Off):
  • Automatically loads the next piece in the setlist when turning past the final page of a score.
  • Return to Setlist on Score End:
  • If continuous reading is disabled, turning past the last page exits back to the setlist view.
  • Show Live Setlist Progress (Toggle On/Off):
  • Enables or disables opening the top progress drawer when tapping the top-center edge of the screen (enabled by default).

docs.title: ✍️ 3. Annotation Settings
docs.text:
The SettingsAnnotationsPage page is divided into two distinct chapters:

  • Chapter 1: Custom Favorite Stickers:
  • Add customized text stickers with any label (e.g., Vibrato, Solo, Mute, Breathe, Look at Conductor).
  • List of active favorites with single-tap deletion ✕.
  • Chapter 2: Active Sticker Categories Selection:
  • Check or uncheck categories to display only the stickers relevant to your playing (Favorites, Fingerings, Dynamics, Articulations, Repeats, Notes, Rests, Accidentals, Symbols).

docs.title: 🦶 4. Bluetooth Pedals & MIDI Controller Settings
docs.text:
The SettingsPedalsPage page delivers streamlined, robust hands-free stage control:

  • Default Active Pedal Profile (Top of Page):
  • Quickly select factory pre-configured profiles: Standard, PageFlip Dragonfly / Firefly / Butterfly, AirTurn Duo / Quad, Joyo, Thomann / Harley Benton, Donner Wireless, IK Multimedia iRig, Coda STOMP, and Advanced MIDI Controller.
  • This profile serves as the application's global default. It applies to all sheet music unless a specific profile is assigned to a setlist.
  • Create new custom profiles and delete with one tap.
  • Stage Safety & Anti-Double Page Turn Protection:
  • « Block fast page turns » Toggle: Prevents accidental multiple page jumps caused by foot switch contact bounce, OS key auto-repeat, or nervous double presses in concert.
  • Adjustable safety debounce delay: 300 ms (Fast), 450 ms (Standard recommended), 600 ms (Concert safe), 800 ms (Strict).
  • Long-Press Sensitivity:
  • Fine-grained slider from 200 ms to 1000 ms to calibrate secondary action triggers on stage.
  • Live Signal Monitor & Diagnostics:
  • Purely event-driven (0% CPU and zero battery drain when idle).
  • Real-time display of incoming signals (Key name, Hex code, Bluetooth/MIDI source, Triggered action).
  • Profile Shortcuts (Collapsible Accordion):
  • Collapsed by default for a clean, non-cluttered interface; expands instantly on tap.
  • Auto-learn mode button (« ➕ Learn a key ») to capture any foot pedal or MIDI command.

docs.title: 🌐 5. App Settings (General)
docs.text:
The SettingsAppPage page handles system settings:

  • 🌐 Multi-Language Selector:
  • Interactive modal with 8 built-in languages:
    • 🇫🇷 Français, 🇬🇧 English, 🇩🇪 Deutsch, 🇪🇸 Español, 🇮🇹 Italiano, 🇵🇱 Polski, 🇳🇱 Nederlands, 🇵🇹 Português.
  • Immediate dynamic translation with no app restart needed.
  • ⚙️ Application Behavior:
  • Show « Quit » tab in bottom navigation (Toggle On/Off):
    • Toggle to display or hide the Quit tab in the main bottom navigation bar. Ideal for musicians relying on Android system gestures or preferring a minimal tab bar.
  • Confirm Before Quitting (Toggle On/Off):
    • Displays a confirmation prompt before closing the app to prevent accidental exit.
  • 📊 Library Metrics & Storage Statistics:
  • Total number of registered PDF scores.
  • Total disk space occupied by sheet music PDFs (in MB/GB).
  • Available storage space: Remaining free capacity on device memory or SD card.
  • SQLite Database Size: Space used by scores.db3 and WAL transaction logs.
  • 📁 Customizable Storage Folders:
  • Scores root folder, audio root folder, and exports root folder.
  • Fully compatible with public Android folders for easy USB file transfer with a PC or Mac.

docs.title: ❓ 6. Built-in Help
docs.text: The HelpPage page includes offline guides and stage troubleshooting tips.

docs.title: ℹ️ 7. About
docs.text: The AboutPage page provides software credits and legal licenses: - Dynamic build version string. - Free software license GNU General Public License v3.0 (GPLv3). - Third-party open-source component credits (.NET MAUI, CommunityToolkit, SQLite, Mozilla PDF.js, SkiaSharp, ZXing). - Direct links to GitHub repository and Privacy Policy.

docs.title: 🛠️ Tools Menu
docs.text: The Tools menu hosts Music Score Manager's powerful suite of built-in utilities designed to manipulate, share, clean up, and safeguard your music catalog completely offline.

docs.title: 📸 1. Score Scanner Studio (High-Definition Paper Scanning)
docs.text:
The Score Scanner (ScoreScannerPage) digitizes physical sheet music directly from your music stand without any external hardware:

  • Instant Camera Capture & Gallery Import:
  • Snap photos of your paper scores directly using your tablet or phone camera (Take Photo), or import previously captured images (Pick Image).
  • High-Visibility Enhancement Filters:
  • B&W High Contrast (Optimized Sheet Music): Applies smart adaptive thresholding to remove stand shadows, whiten the paper background, and make staves and musical notes razor-sharp.
  • Grayscale: Smooths tonal gradients while maintaining a compact file size.
  • Original Color: Preserves the natural warm paper color and handwritten pencil or highlighter annotations.
  • Musical Metadata & Folder / Category Assignment:
  • Fill in the Score Title and Composer / Arranger right away.
  • Folder / Category Selection: Pick the target folder (defaults to "Général") or tap ➕ to create a new folder on the fly.
  • Dynamic Multi-Page Management:
  • Thumbnail preview of every page with index counters.
  • Individual 90° rotation (↻) and targeted deletion (🗑️).
  • Delete All button to reset the current scanning session if needed.
  • Instant Multi-Page PDF Generation:
  • Tap Generate Score (available at the top header and bottom of the page) to compile all processed pages into a multi-page PDF, register it in your library, and open it immediately in the performance viewer!

docs.title: 📑 2. PDF Creator & Assembler Studio
docs.text: The PDF Assembler Studio (PdfAssemblerPage) is an all-in-one document manipulation studio built right into the app.

docs.title: Key Capabilities:
docs.text:
• Build PDFs from Photos or Scans:
  • Select photos of sheet music from your gallery or camera (.jpg, .png).
  • Compiles them into a crisp, high-resolution PDF document preserving 100% of their aspect ratio.
  • Modify Existing Scores or External PDFs:
  • Load any piece from your library or any external PDF document directly into the studio.
  • Merge Additional Sheets or Photos:
  • Insert additional photos (➕ Photos) or merge pages from another PDF file (➕ PDF).
  • Insert Blank Pages (📄 Blank Page):
  • Strategic feature to synchronize page turns on physical music stands and dual-page landscape views.
  • Interactive Page Thumbnails:
  • View miniature previews of every page with its sequence index number.
  • Rearrange Pages:
  • Use Move Up (▲) and Move Down (▼) buttons to reorder pages intuitively.
  • Individual Page Rotations:
  • Tap ↻ Rotate on any specific page thumbnail to turn it in 90° steps (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°). Perfect for correcting sideways scans.
  • Duplicate Pages:
  • Clone any page with a single tap (ideal for repeated chorus sections or Da Capo jumps without turning back).
  • Delete Pages (🗑️):
  • Remove cover pages, blank sheets, or unwanted download advertisements.
  • Reverse All Pages:
  • Quickly fixes sheet music scanned in backwards order.
  • Rotate Entire Document:
  • Single-tap 90° rotation across all pages in the document.
  • High-Definition Page Preview:
  • Tap the magnifying glass icon or the thumbnail to preview any page in full screen with interactive zoom and rotation.
  • Save as New or Overwrite:
  • Save as a brand new score or overwrite the original PDF directly in your library while preserving all metadata and ratings.

docs.title: 📡 3. Wi-Fi Direct Transfer (P2P) & Group Broadcast
docs.text: The Wi-Fi Direct Transfer module (WifiTransferPage) powers direct wireless sharing between devices with no external internet, router, or mobile data required. Received scores and setlists are automatically placed into the default "Général" folder, preserving each musician's customized directory structure without imposing the sender's hierarchy.

docs.title: A. Direct Tablet-to-Tablet Transfer (P2P):
docs.text:
1. Receiver:
  2. Opens Tools > Wi-Fi Direct Transfer, enables Wi-Fi, and taps « 🟢 Receive Mode (Make Visible) ». The device enters discoverable mode.
  3. Sender:
  4. Picks a score or setlist to share.
  5. Selects whether to bundle personal annotations and audio tracks.
  6. Selects the target recipient from the discovered devices list. The binary stream transfers in seconds over local TCP sockets.
  7. Acceptance:
  8. Receiver taps Accept on the confirmation prompt, and items integrate immediately into the library.

docs.title: B. Multi-Musician Group Broadcast (QR Code):
docs.text:
1. The Band Leader / Conductor (Sender):
  2. Selects the setlist or pieces to share and taps « 📲 Group Broadcast Mode (QR Code) ».
  3. The app starts an ad-hoc local server and displays a large QR Code on screen with a live connected musicians counter.
  4. Group Musicians (Receivers):
  5. Open Tools > Wi-Fi Direct Transfer and scan the QR Code on the leader's tablet.
  6. All band members download the score or complete setlist in parallel simultaneously without needing an internet router!

docs.title: 🏷️ 4. Tag Management
docs.text: The Tag Management screen (TagsPage & TagEditPage) gives you full control over library categorization: - Create New Tags with custom names (e.g., Choir, Sight Reading, Christmas Concert, Lead Sheet). - RGB Color Palette & Sliders: Choose predefined colors or mix custom colors using Red, Green, and Blue sliders with real-time badge preview. - Search, Edit & Rename existing tags. - Delete Tags: Safely removes tags without deleting any underlying sheet music files.

docs.title: 📦 5. Package & Setlist Imports
docs.text: The Package Import tool (ImportPackagePage) handles external archives: - Supported Formats: .msmsetlist (complete setlist), .msmscore (individual score with annotations/audio), and .msmscores (batch archive of multiple pieces). - Automated Extraction: Extracts PDFs, recreates musical metadata (composer, key, tempo, rating), restores drawings/annotations, and attaches audio files automatically. - Neutral Destination: Files extracted from imported packages are stored in the default "Général" category to maintain clean organization.

docs.title: 🔍 6. Duplicate Finder
docs.text: The Duplicate Finder (DuplicatesPage) audits your library storage to free up disk space: - SHA-256 Cryptographic Hash Check: Compares the exact binary contents and byte length of PDF files, catching duplicates even if filenames or titles differ. - Recursive Folder Scanning: Recursively inspects all category sub-directories (📁 [Category] Path). - Side-by-Side Duplicate Groups: Displays matching files with their file sizes, dates, and wasted storage space. - Safe Cleaning: Delete redundant copies while keeping the original library entry intact.

docs.title: 💾 7. Database Backups & Restoration
docs.text: The Backups utility (BackupsPage) ensures your annotations and organization are never lost: - Instant Database Snapshot: Create a dated backup of your SQLite database (scores.db3 containing scores, setlists, tags, links, annotations). - Database Backup History: View and restore database snapshots in 1 click. - Automated Backup Scheduling: - Configurable interval in days (e.g., every 30 days). - Maximum retention limit with automated rotation (e.g., keep the 6 most recent backups). - Complete Data Backup (.zip): All-in-one compressed .zip export packaging the SQLite database, all physical PDF scores with their category folder structures, and all attached audio backing tracks. - Customizable Destination: Defaults to the device's Download directory and can be redirected to external storage (USB drive, SD card) or cloud storage (Google Drive, pCloud, OneDrive). - Blocking Progress Overlay: Step-by-step progress tracking with exact percentage and safe cancellation support. - Complete Restore (Erase / Replace): Full re-import from a backup .zip with solemn confirmation, safe cache staging extraction, complete replacement, and post-restore integrity validation.

docs.title: 📖 Fullscreen Sheet Music Viewer (Stage Mode)
docs.text: The Viewer (ViewerPage) is where music comes to life. Tailored to eliminate all visual distractions, it offers maximum readability, zero-flash synchronous rendering, and rapid gesture and hardware controls.

docs.title: 👆 Stage Gestures & Navigation
docs.text:
• Turn to Next Page:
  • Tap the right half of the screen or swipe right-to-left (fully configurable in Settings: horizontal swipe, tap, or vertical swipe).
  • Turn to Previous Page:
  • Tap the left half or swipe left-to-right.
  • Continuous Setlist Transition:
  • When reaching the final page of a score in a setlist, the next page turn immediately opens page 1 of the next piece.
  • Pinch-to-Zoom & Smooth Pan:
  • Spread two fingers to enlarge a tight measure or complex notation. Freely pan around the score even while zoomed.
  • 2-Page Landscape View:
  • On horizontal tablet screens, enable dual-page mode in Settings to display two consecutive pages side by side.
  • Annotations are projected with millimeter geometric accuracy on left (leftPage) and right (rightPage) pages, respecting letterbox and pillarbox margins.
  • Clickable Page Indicator:
  • Bottom-right page count badge (e.g., 2/8). Tapping it opens a direct jump dialog to any page number.

docs.title: 🦶 Hands-Free Foot Control: Bluetooth Pedals & MIDI Events
docs.text: Music Score Manager features universal hardware controller support: - Bluetooth HID Pedals & Wireless Keyboards: AirTurn, PageFlip Dragonfly/Firefly, Joyo, Donner, Thomann/Harley Benton, IK Multimedia iRig BlueTurn, Coda STOMP, standard keyboard arrows, etc. - MIDI Controllers (USB-OTG & Bluetooth MIDI): Sustain pedals (CC 64), sostenuto (CC 66), soft pedals (CC 67), MIDI note events, and Program Changes. - Assignable Stage Actions (independently assignable to short press or long press with 200–1000 ms sensitivity): - Next / previous page - Next / previous song in setlist - Song start (page 1) / song end - Scroll up / down - Start / stop metronome & mute sound - Backing audio Play / Pause / Restart - Reset zoom to 100% - Open direct page jump - Lock / unlock annotations - Undo / Redo annotations - Open central menu / Close viewer

docs.title: 🛠️ Quick Tools Drawer (Top-Right)
docs.text:
Tap the top-right corner of the screen (or the [ 🛠️ ] icon if enabled in settings) to open the Quick Tools Drawer. It lets you toggle stage components instantaneously in real time without interrupting playback:

  1. ✍️ Annotations: Shows or hides the bottom annotation toolbar.
  2. ⏱️ Metronome: Expands or collapses the synchronized visual metronome.
  3. 🎧 Audio Player: Shows or hides the floating backing track transport bar.
  4. 📄 Page Number: Toggles the bottom-right page indicator.
  5. 🎛️ Tuner: Launches the floating multi-instrument precision tuner.
  6. 🏷️ Score Title: Toggles the top title bar showing the active piece name.

All toggles update live dynamically on screen immediately upon tapping.

docs.title: 🎛️ High-Precision Multi-Instrument Tuner
docs.text:
Music Score Manager includes a professional stage-grade chromatic tuner accessible directly during rehearsals or live performances without leaving your score:

  • Movable & Draggable Floating Panel:
  • Equipped with a dedicated tactile drag handle ⠿ Move and smooth pan gesture: reposition the tuner anywhere on screen so it never covers critical bars or notes.
  • Fast-close ✕ button in the top right.
  • State-of-the-Art DSP Engine (YIN Algorithm):
  • YIN Pitch Detection ($\theta = 0.15$): Computes cumulative mean normalized difference $d'(\tau)$ for pinpoint pitch accuracy, eradicating octave jumping and false harmonics.
  • 2-Pole Low-Pass Filter (1200 Hz): Eliminates breath noise, reed sizzle on woodwinds, and sharp pick attack transients.
  • Smart Sub-Harmonic & Octave Correction: Resolves fundamental masking common to acoustic instruments whose fundamental ($f_0$) is overshadowed by the 2nd or 3rd harmonic (saxophones, French horn, bassoon, oboe, cello, double bass).
  • Sliding Median Filter & Exponential Needle Smoothing (EMA): Rock-solid cents needle response with zero visual jitter ($\alpha = 0.45$).
  • Diapason Reference Calibration (A4 Frequency):
  • Fine-tune reference pitch from Baroque (415 Hz), Natural pitch (432 Hz), International standard (440 Hz), Symphonic orchestra (442 Hz), up to 444 Hz.
  • Extensive Instrument Library & Tailored Presets:
  • Universal Chromatic Tuner: Detects all 12 semitones across all octaves with exact frequency readout in Hz.
  • Guitars & Basses: Standard Guitar (E A D G B E), 4-string Bass (E A D G), 5-string Bass (B E A D G).
  • Bowed Strings & Folk: Violin (G D A E), Viola (C G D A), Cello (C G D A), Double Bass (E A D G), Ukulele (G C E A), 5-string Banjo (Open G).
  • Saxophone Family (Full Quartet): Alto Saxophone (in E♭), Tenor Saxophone (in B♭), Baritone Saxophone (in E♭), Soprano Saxophone (in B♭).
  • Brass & Harmony Winds: Trumpet & Clarinet (in B♭), French Horn (in F), Trombone / Euphonium / Tuba (in C - Bass Clef).
  • Woodwinds: Concert Flute (in C), Oboe & Bassoon (in C, including the Oboe A 440 Hz benchmark for orchestral tuning).
  • Vocals & Singing: Dedicated singing ranges and warmup benchmark notes (Bass, Baritone, Tenor, Alto, Mezzo, Soprano).
  • Intuitive Visual Gauge:
  • Calibrated cents arc (-50 to +50 cents) with dynamic color feedback (Green = in tune, Amber/Red = flat or sharp).
  • Dual note name display (Standard A, B, C... and classical Solfège Do, Ré, Mi...), octave index, and precise live frequency in Hz.

docs.title: 🎛️ Central Quick Menu (Double-Tap)
docs.text:
Double-tap at the center of the screen to open the quick action menu without leaving your score:

  1. ↻ Rotation (+90°):
  2. Rotates the score clockwise by 90 degrees.
  3. « Apply to this page only » toggle: Rotate only an inverted landscape page.
  4. « Remember rotations » toggle: Saves orientation permanently in SQLite.
  5. 🔍 Reset zoom to 100%:
  6. Instantly restores default full-page scaling and centers the document.
  7. 📄 Page: Jump directly to a page number.
  8. ⏱️ Show / Hide Metronome: Toggles the metronome overlay.
  9. 🎧 Show / Hide Audio Player: Toggles the audio transport overlay.
  10. 📑 Modify PDF Assembly: Direct shortcut to PDF Assembler Studio.
  11. ✏️ Edit Score: Instant access to musical metadata editing.
  12. Return to Home / Close: Clean exit from the viewer.

docs.title: ✍️ Complete Annotation Suite
docs.text:
The annotation toolbar expands from the bottom of the screen and adapts effortlessly to your movements:

  • Dedicated Vertical Pan Handle (⠿):
  • Located at the left of the toolbar, the ⠿ handle allows smooth vertical sliding across the screen without conflicting with horizontal tool scrolling.
  • Smartphone & Mobile Responsiveness:
  • On phones, the close button ✕ is fixed to the right edge so it remains instantly accessible regardless of screen width.
  • 🖌️ Chiseled Highlighter (Stabilo):
  • Natural translucent stroke with flat, chiseled ends (PenLineCap.Flat).
  • 4 vibrant colors (yellow, green, blue, pink) and 3 widths (5 mm, 10 mm, 18 mm).
  • T Typographic Text:
  • Place custom typed text directly on the sheet music, 6 colors, 5 font sizes.
  • ✎ Freehand Pencil:
  • 100% opaque foreground drawing, 6 solid colors, 5 calibrated widths from 1 mm to 5 mm.
  • ❏ Musical Stickers & Favorites:
  • Over 100 stickers organized into categories: Favorites, Fingerings, Dynamics, Articulations, Repeats, Notes (𝅝, 𝅗𝅥, ♩, ♪, ♫...), Rests (𝄻, 𝄼, 𝄽, 𝄾...), Accidentals (♯, ♭, ♮, 𝄪, 𝄫), and Symbols.
  • Large tactile slider to effortlessly adjust sticker size with your fingers.
  • ↩️ Undo & ↪️ Redo:
  • Dynamic step-by-step history to quickly reverse or reapply any drawing or sticker placement.
  • 🔒/🔓 Strict Safety Lock:
  • Automatically locks by default on score open to safeguard the score from unwanted touches during live play.
  • Automatically unlocks when selecting an editing tool.
  • Automatically relocks when closing the toolbar (cross button ✕).
  • ✧ Clear Page: Reset all annotations on the current page with safety confirmation.
  • 🗑️ Targeted Delete: Touch any existing sticker or text to modify or delete it.

docs.title: ⏱️ High-Precision Built-in Metronome
docs.text:
• Thread-Safe Regulated Engine: Zero CPU drift via double timing loop (Stopwatch + SpinWait).
  • Zero Audio Latency: Direct hardware sample triggers via Android SoundPool.
  • Visual Pulse & LED: Flashing LED indicator synchronized with downbeats and upbeats.
  • Audio Click Mute: Toggle sound on/off on the fly while retaining visual pulsing.
  • Synchronized Pre-Count: Precise measure countdown before starting audio playback.

docs.title: 🎧 Synchronized Audio Backing Player
docs.text:
• Supports attached MP3, WAV, AAC, and FLAC accompaniment tracks.
  • Compact transport bar with Play/Pause button.
  • Scrubbing progress slider with elapsed time and total duration display.
  • Floating and freely draggable anywhere on the screen.
